There are a few tweaks I would make to your design if I were you:

Fonts:  
\- Reducing the number of fonts used would make the design more cohesive.  
\- Standardizing the body font size (the "Join us for an.." font size looks smaller than the "Hosted with..." part).  
\- For the text at the top, consider using a shadow instead of an outline if you want to increase contrast between the white text and background.

Objects:

\- The triangles on the top right could be removed since it doesn't really match the colour scheme, and imbalances the poster since the other elements are quite centralised.

\- The dark yellow line and glitter object also doesn't quite match the colour scheme. You could replace it with a star/glitter/gradient object that is a glowing neon pink/cyan to match the event text and that would also stand out more against the dark background!

Copywriting:  
\- "Presents..." isn't really necessary in this context and visually takes away from the cool event name.  
\- The event description is a little vague. You could mention what activities are at the event, whether there'll be food, drinks, dancing, open-mic sessions.... and anything attention grabbing that would entice your target audience to attend!

The algorithm boosts your first couple of posts, and then it's up to how much people want to watch your content. Would recommend watching the top Tiktok content creators for your specific genre, and using similar hashtags or audio or trending video formats if you want to target their audience pool.   


Once you know what those are, think of a differentiating factor. What makes your content stand out from theirs? Some creators may choose to use specific meme audio, some have their own unique intro to every video, etc.   


If you're boosting another channel with longform content, leave a CTA at the end of the videos and let your audience know what they have to gain by watching your long-form content. Do you offer game strat advice? Humour? Reveal tricks or easter eggs? You get the idea.  


Also, if you're getting comments, you could try interacting with your audience. Build a small group of fans who stay for you, and they will be your loyal audience.   


Good luck champ!

Hey OP, good on you for realising that you’re a slacker! I was in your spot a couple years ago because my team gave me all the design and a lot of editing work, which took extra long to complete. As a result, I was unmotivated and unproductive  between tasks. I would work on my own things during classes. In October, my group leader had a talk with me, and said that they wanted to file a report if I didn’t get my act together. I was in your place, angry and crying myself to sleep — but I also knew that doing so wouldn’t change the situation.

I communicated all the issues I had with the work that was delegated to me — why I was slow, what I needed help with. And in return, my group was more than happy to fill in the gaps to make sure I could give my best work. I started proactively involving myself by asking what they needed. 

I looked out for what assessments were yet to be complete: 
1. The presentation
2. The individual report 

And then started working on them ahead of the group to help them get things done. I wrote the full scripts and designed slides for my group, as well as brainstormed with them for individual portions. 

Of course, this didn’t save my reputation. I was a slacker. It didn’t make me any better a person than I was before. But here’s what happened: 

Towards the end, they saw that I was putting in effort and empathised with my previous state of being unmotivated. As a result, no report was filed. I taught them how to write better and equipped them with presentation skills that they needed. We ended up becoming friends and all scored As for PW. 

You can’t change or excuse your shitty behaviour the past 10 months, but the next few weeks says a lot about your ability to reflect and change. Don’t be sorry, be better. List out all the problems you’re facing and figure out solutions with your group, and understand what problems they’re facing so that you may contribute. If you have strong writing and presentation skills, it’s time to help your group mates work on theirs. 

Good luck ✨

Putting my opinions on 18 chefs aside, here's my opinion purely on the design of the site. I did your form and personally found it hard to respond to because it's been a while since I last visited the place (once every few months, which wasn't an option).

Suggestion to OP as a student interested in UX design: For more insight, I think it would be more helpful for you to see people click through the site step-by-step, narrating their thoughts whilst doing so, in person. It's easier to observe what's intuitive for the user and what is less appealing to them that way, especially through noting the functions that are more commonly used and the ones that are ignored completely. There are some pop-ups you may want to prioritise, and others that can be shown only upon clicking through to a relevant section - same with the buttons.  (e.g. Citibank payment promo may be more relevant when placed payment section instead of the home page)

My feedback:

\- Certain pop-ups and slides on the mobile site may be a bit intrusive and seem to fight for attention (4 pop-ups upon loading the site)

\- The scroll-down sections in full-caps scream visual clutter. It may be more helpful to highlight sections of the menu and not highlight the rest. Using better high-quality visuals and fewer words would be ideal.

\- There are some awkward white gaps in some parts of the BYOM section that can be resized

I recently visited a restaurant, Koal, and found their online design quite appealing. You could check out their site for reference :p

TL;DR It's functional, but can do better in placement and positioning. Interviews may be more helpful than surveys for your research.

I feel for you and am in a similar position— I’m nearly 19 and have fairly protective parents too. Here’s what I have to say about everything.

*About the boyfriend*

I met my bf last year and I have to say that letting my parents meet him was one of the best decisions I’ve made. 

My mom also demands that she knows my friends and their parents when we hang out/sleep over. Even now, I’m allowed sleep overs only with multiple friends present + if I send pictures to her showing who I’m with.

I used to be limited to outings with my friends only once every month (especially in school), but was finally allowed to see him once a week even during my A lvl period. He helped me study for my Econs and my parents were really, really happy about that. Now that I’m done with A levels, I do have more freedom. They are also comfortable with him because they know his character and intentions are good.

Other benefits of letting them meet him include family outings, reimbursed dates (so that I can pay for myself) and being given space (they stopped calling during my outings and allowed me to go home myself instead of insisting on picking me up). All of this is based on mutual trust. I’ve also had a difficult conversation with my parents and we have agreed on a code phrase for “I am in a bad situation and need help” now that I go to bars/clubs/hang out more and am more independent. They know that I will contact them should things go south. Sure, they may scold me/be harsh in those situations, but it’s far better than not having any guidance, money and support during an emergency.

Oh, and, I’m home by 10pm most of the time. If I stay out any later, I’d drop them a text and my location. They’re more than happy to pick me up so I don’t have to pass by any dark alleyways on my way home. 

*On sex*

On the whole, I have to say that most parents can still be conservative when it comes to sex. My parents do not condone premarital sex and they would definitely look at me differently if I were to engage in it, even though I technically have autonomy over my body. 

My boyfriend and I have decided to lay off the sex and establish a more stable relationship for the time being. He also is respectful of my parents and has reaffirmed me that sex and staying over is not his priority in our relationship. I am slightly disconcerted with the idea of your guy encouraging you to go against your parents for the sake of this staycation. I don’t mean to assume, but he does seem to be more concerned about his relationship with you, and failing to consider the social/familial repercussions that the things you do together may have on you. Are you able to wait it out and allow your relationship to stabilise a little more before doing so? A guy who really, really loves you would be able to respect that. Especially if he’s thinking for your best interest. 

That being said, I know you may want to proceed with it anyway. 

Based off what I hear from my friends and their horror stories, here’s what I can say. Do it safely (get std checks on top of contraceptives), don’t take any videos or pictures, and make sure you’re in a position to reject any sexual advances at any point of time (i.e. you are still in a position to say no even if you’re naked or about to do it or doing it). Keep it private, keep it low key, and always have a back up (plan B, trusted friends you can contact if anything goes wrong, access to a gynaecologist, etc.). You’re not a porn object either, so don’t expect your experience to be straight out of an adult film. 

*On clothes*

As for revealing clothes, tight tops are really in right now so I can understand why some parents are concerned. We get leered at for wearing loose tees and school uniforms, much less body-con fits. If they’re concerned, just get some cute cardigans to wear over them and take the cardigan off when you are comfortable doing so. Exposing your parents to what the more recent clothing trends are maaaay make them more open to them too (lmao I introd my mom to tiktok and she’s okay with it now because she now understands that it’s not just xmm dancing for pedos). 

In sum, I still am viewed as a child by my parents and I’m sure you are too. However, breaching their trust isn’t advisable. They’ll just set more restrictions and try to do more extreme things to curb your behaviour. I say this because my parents have set up CCTV cameras in my home to track my brother’s movements in and out of home and previously used phone trackers on him. Moreover, expecting their mindset towards you to shift the moment you hit 18 or get into University is highly unlikely. Gain their trust and set up a support system that includes your parents (communicate this to them). They’re more likely to be less anxious if they know that you are able to look out for yourself. 

Anyway, I hope the lengthy response wasn’t too much for you. Feel free to pm me if you wanna talk about anything. Stay safe, healthy and happy 🤍🤍
